Proximity input to E00 Hz

E0: closer obstacles produce a higher pulse rate (0–40 Hz). Proximity is 0 outside the look-ahead and approaches 1 near contact. E1 encodes grounded / airborne state. Input updates every 50 ms; neurons integrate every 1 ms.

Miss: random sensory feedback for 1 s. Clear: predictable sensory feedback for 0.5 s. Both enter E0–E1. No extra rest.

Research settings

These are experiment parameters, not learned values. Step advances 50 ms of simulated time; it is not a hardware latency.

Look-ahead sets how far into the approaching scene the sensor responds. The decoder jumps when pooled E2–E5 firing reaches the chosen rate. Feedback changes sensory input; the current learning rule changes weights through spike timing, without a signed reward multiplier.

Neural activity · 32 cells

Rows N0–N31 are individual neurons. Each mark is a spike counted in a recorded bin; left to right is the last 5 seconds of neural time. E0–E7 each pool four cells. E0–E1 receive input; E2–E5 drive jumps; E6–E7 are context recording pools.

Trial 1 ·

Neuron characteristics and connections

32 simulated leaky integrate-and-fire cells: 24 excitatory and 8 inhibitory. Each connection has a weight; a neuron does not have one single weight.
